metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (Python/Django) with a deployable entry point (Django web app with ROOT_URLCONF and views) and database configuration present. Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: Database connections present (PostgreSQL configured in settings.py with read/write operations). Views perform CRUD-like operations on tickets. No multi-service orchestration, no event consumption. Classified as stateful-crud.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Overall score 1.18 falls in the Not Ready band (< 1.5) but 11 High findings yield Remediation Required tier (2-11 High). Divergence caused by surface-flag exclusions reducing evaluable core questions: 3 core questions (DATA-Q4=pass, SEC-Q1=Not Evaluated, OPS-Q5=Not Evaluated) do not emit High findings, capping achievable High count at 11 — below the ≥12 threshold for count-based Not Ready.

decomposition_strategy.rationale: The codebase is extremely small (2 source files, ~50 lines). Upgrade technology stack first, then strengthen as modular monolith with proper Django patterns before considering service extraction.

effort_factors.cicd_maturity: None (high effort — pipeline must be built first)

findings.title: No managed compute — all workloads on raw EC2
findings.description: All compute runs on a single raw EC2 instance (Ubuntu 12.04 EOL) with Apache 2.2 + mod_wsgi. No managed container orchestration or serverless.
findings.gap: No managed compute — 100% raw EC2 with manual server management.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to ECS/Fargate or Lambda after containerizing the application. First upgrade Python/Django stack, then create a Dockerfile, then deploy to managed compute.

findings.title: Self-managed PostgreSQL on same EC2 instance
findings.description: PostgreSQL 9.1 runs self-managed on the same EC2 instance as the application (HOST: 127.0.0.1). No managed database service, no automated failover, no multi-AZ.
findings.gap: Database is entirely self-managed on a single EC2 instance with no managed services.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL or Aurora PostgreSQL. Upgrade from PostgreSQL 9.1 (EOL) to a current supported version.

findings.title: No workflow orchestration for ticket lifecycle
findings.description: No workflow orchestration service in use. Ticket lifecycle handled entirely through hardcoded application logic. For a stateful-crud archetype, this represents missing orchestration for ticket lifecycle workflows.
findings.gap: No orchestration — all workflow logic hardcoded in application code.
findings.recommendation: Consider AWS Step Functions for ticket lifecycle workflows (assignment routing, escalation, SLA enforcement) as the application matures. Lower priority than compute, database, and DevOps modernization.

findings.title: No messaging or streaming infrastructure
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure. All communication is synchronous. For a stateful-crud helpdesk system, state changes (ticket created, assigned, resolved) should emit events for notifications and integrations.
findings.gap: No messaging where state changes cross service boundaries — tight synchronous coupling. Email notifications handled synchronously via SMTP.
findings.recommendation: Introduce SQS or EventBridge for ticket lifecycle events. This enables decoupled notification delivery and future integrations.

findings.title: No network security configuration
findings.description: No VPC configuration, no security groups, no network segmentation. Application and database co-located on single instance with no network separation between tiers.
findings.gap: No evidence of VPC, private subnets, or security groups. No network segmentation.
findings.recommendation: Deploy in a VPC with private subnets, separate application and database tiers, configure least-privilege security groups.

findings.title: No managed API entry point
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, CloudFront, or any managed entry point. Application served directly by Apache 2.2 on EC2 with no load balancer, no throttling, no request validation.
findings.gap: Services exposed directly with no gateway or load balancer.
findings.recommendation: Add an ALB or API Gateway as the entry point for health checks, throttling, TLS termination, and request routing.

findings.title: No auto-scaling configured
findings.description: No auto-scaling. Single EC2 instance with no ASG, no dynamic capacity management. All capacity statically provisioned.
findings.gap: No auto-scaling — all capacity is statically provisioned on a single instance.
findings.recommendation: After containerizing, configure auto-scaling on ECS/Fargate or use Lambda for automatic scaling.

findings.title: Inadequate backup and recovery
findings.description: Only a manual pg_dump cron exists with no defined retention, no PITR, no tested restore procedures, no cross-region replication.
findings.gap: Manual pg_dump cron only — no defined retention, no tested restore, no PITR.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to RDS PostgreSQL for automated backups with configurable retention and PITR.

findings.title: Zero Infrastructure as Code coverage
findings.description: 0% IaC coverage. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, or any IaC files. All infrastructure manually created.
findings.gap: No IaC — all infrastructure created manually (ClickOps).
findings.recommendation: Adopt IaC immediately (Terraform or CDK). This is a prerequisite for all other modernization efforts.

findings.title: No CI/CD automation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipelines. Deployment is 'git pull on the server + manual apache restart'. No automated testing, no build stage, no deployment automation.
findings.gap: No CI/CD — all deployments are manual.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions, CodePipeline, or GitLab CI) with build, test, and deploy stages.

findings.title: End-of-life language and framework
findings.description: Python 2.7 (EOL January 2020) with Django 1.4 (EOL 2015). Compound legacy — both language version AND framework are end-of-life.
findings.gap: Compound legacy — language version AND framework both regressed and end-of-life.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to Python 3.12+ with Django 5.x. This is a prerequisite for all other modernization.

findings.title: Tightly-coupled monolith with no module boundaries
findings.description: Tightly-coupled monolith with raw SQL in views, no models.py, no separation of concerns. All state shared via single PostgreSQL database on localhost.
findings.gap: Tightly-coupled monolith with no clear module boundaries, pervasive shared state.
findings.recommendation: See Decomposition Strategy. Upgrade technology stack first, then restructure with proper Django patterns before considering service extraction.

findings.title: All communication synchronous with no async patterns
findings.description: All communication is synchronous HTTP. No async patterns, no message publishing, no event-driven handlers. For a stateful-crud helpdesk application, ticket state changes should emit events for notifications and integrations.
findings.gap: All communication synchronous HTTP with no async patterns.
findings.recommendation: Introduce event-driven patterns for ticket lifecycle events using SQS or EventBridge after modernizing the stack.

findings.title: No long-running process handling
findings.description: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. No background job framework, no async/polling patterns, no job status APIs.
findings.gap: All operations synchronous regardless of duration — no async job processing capability.
findings.recommendation: Add background job framework (Celery with SQS, or Lambda async) for operations that may exceed 30 seconds.

findings.title: No API versioning strategy
findings.description: No API versioning. No /v1/ URL patterns, no version headers, no versioning annotations.
findings.gap: No versioning — breaking changes deployed directly.
findings.recommendation: Implement URL-path versioning (/v1/) when rebuilding the API layer.

findings.title: All endpoints hard-coded
findings.description: All service endpoints hard-coded: database at 127.0.0.1:5432, email at exchange.acme-corp.internal:25. No environment variables, no service registry.
findings.gap: All service endpoints hard-coded in application code/configuration.
findings.recommendation: Externalize configuration using environment variables or AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.

findings.title: Unstructured data on local filesystem
findings.description: Static files served from local disk with no CDN, no S3, no managed object storage, no parsing pipeline.
findings.gap: Data on local file systems with no managed storage, no CDN, no parsing capabilities.
findings.recommendation: Migrate static files and attachments to Amazon S3. Add CloudFront as CDN for static assets.

findings.title: No data access layer — raw SQL scattered in views
findings.description: No data access layer. Raw SQL queries with string formatting scattered directly in views.py. Django ORM not used despite being available.
findings.gap: Database imports and queries scattered across views with no pattern.
findings.recommendation: Replace raw SQL with Django ORM models. Implement proper data access layer. This also eliminates SQL injection vulnerabilities.

findings.title: Database engine at EOL (PostgreSQL 9.1)
findings.description: PostgreSQL 9.1 reached end-of-life in November 2016 — over 8 years ago. No version pinning in IaC, no upgrade procedure.
findings.gap: Database engine at EOL (PostgreSQL 9.1, EOL November 2016). No version management.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to PostgreSQL 15+ combined with migration to RDS for managed version lifecycle.

findings.title: No encryption at rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest configured. PostgreSQL on local disk with no KMS, no EBS encryption. Static files on local disk with no encryption.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest configured for any data store.
findings.recommendation: Enable encryption at rest with KMS when migrating to RDS and S3.

findings.title: No API authentication on endpoints
findings.description: No authentication on ticket views. No @login_required decorators, no permission checks, no token validation. Endpoints are open to unauthenticated access.
findings.gap: No API authentication — endpoints are open.
findings.recommendation: Add @login_required immediately. When modernizing, implement OAuth2/JWT via Cognito or API Gateway authorizers.

findings.title: No centralized identity integration
findings.description: Application uses Django built-in auth with no external IdP. No OIDC/SAML, no Cognito, no SSO.
findings.gap: Application manages own authentication with no external IdP integration.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with centralized IdP (Amazon Cognito or corporate SAML/OIDC) for SSO.

findings.title: Plaintext credentials in source code
findings.description: SECRET_KEY and database PASSWORD committed to settings.py in plaintext. Visible to anyone with repository access and persists in git history.
findings.gap: Critical — plaintext credentials in source code committed to version control.
findings.recommendation: Immediately rotate all exposed credentials. Move secrets to AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation.

findings.title: No compute hardening or patching
findings.description: No patching strategy, no vulnerability scanning. Server runs Ubuntu 12.04 (EOL April 2017) with no security updates for over 7 years.
findings.gap: No patching strategy, no vulnerability scanning, running on EOL OS.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to supported OS (Amazon Linux 2023 or Ubuntu 22.04+). Implement SSM Patch Manager. Consider Fargate to eliminate OS patching.

findings.title: No application security pipeline
findings.description: No SAST, DAST, or dependency scanning. No CI/CD pipeline to integrate security tools. Known SQL injection and XSS vulnerabilities undetected.
findings.gap: No security scanning tools — no pipeline exists to integrate them into.
findings.recommendation: Include SAST (Semgrep), dependency scanning (pip-audit), and container scanning in the CI/CD pipeline when implemented.

findings.title: No distributed tracing
findings.description: No tracing instrumented. No X-Ray, no OpenTelemetry. Only debugging mechanism is a Python 2 print statement.
findings.gap: No distributed tracing — no observability into request flows.
findings.recommendation: Add OpenTelemetry instrumentation with X-Ray after modernizing the stack.

findings.title: No SLO definitions
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No CloudWatch alarms, no latency monitoring, no error rate tracking, no availability targets.
findings.gap: No SLOs — no formal definition of acceptable service levels.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs (availability, p95/p99 response time, error rate) and implement CloudWatch alarms after infrastructure modernization.

findings.title: No business metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No business metrics (ticket resolution time, volume, SLA compliance). No dashboards.
findings.gap: No custom metrics — no business outcome tracking.
findings.recommendation: Publish business metrics (tickets created/resolved, mean resolution time, SLA compliance) to CloudWatch after modernizing.

findings.title: No anomaly detection or alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection. Failures detected only when users report them.
findings.gap: No alerting configured — failures detected only reactively.
findings.recommendation: Implement CloudWatch alarms for error rates and response times. Add anomaly detection on critical paths.

findings.title: No integration tests
findings.description: No test files exist in the repository. No test framework configured, no CI pipeline to run tests.
findings.gap: No integration tests — no automated tests at all.
findings.recommendation: Add integration tests using Django test framework or pytest-django. Include in CI/CD pipeline.

findings.title: No observability ownership
findings.description: No dashboards, no alarms with named owners, no CODEOWNERS. Only the ADMINS tuple in settings.py (Django error email recipient).
findings.gap: No observability ownership — monitoring is reactive and fragmented.
findings.recommendation: Define service ownership with CODEOWNERS. Create per-service dashboards with named owners once on managed infrastructure.
